Dr Patrica Jones
Paediatrics Ward Doctor
East hospital
UK

05.09.2019

Re: Eleanor Holmes, aged 8 years

Dear Dr Jones,

I am writing to transfer Eleanor, who was admitted into South Park Hospital in Spain after a near-
drowning accident with a potential hypoxic brain injury, into your care. I would be grateful if you
could carry on her management plan.

On 24.08.2019, Eleanor was attended by paramedics 15 to 20 minutes after she had fallen into a
freshwater lake in Barcelona whilst she was on holiday with her father. She was found cyanotic,
pulseless and apnoeic; thus, CPR was performed, and she was put on a ventilator when admitted to
our hospital. [missing: She was also hypothaermic with fixed dilated pupil <– condition after the
accident should be written in detail] Over the following weeks, the condition improved as she was
gradually weaned off the mechanical ventilation. However, she has begun to experience cough
with a pink expectoration, dysarthria, concentration difficulties and headaches for which
paracetamol was prescribed.

Consequently, further monitoring of Eleanor’s cough and headaches would be appreciated.
Continuing speech therapy for dysarthria as well as organising neurological examination; including,
neuropsychological evaluation, visual-spatial testing, IQ testing and checking for the possibility of
any delayed problem are recommended. Additionally, the probable sequelae of hypoxia need to be
discussed with her parents.

If you have any questions, please contact me.

Yours sincerely,
Doctor
